newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks erase losses at close, eyeing U.S..
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks erase losses at close, eyeing U.S..

text.p: Madrid stocks managed to iron out heavy intraday losses by the close on Tuesday, taking heart from a strong rise on Wall Street, dealers said.
Short-term, lighter volumes and volatility are likely to characterise trading amid doubts over Europe's single currency. Nevertheless the market is not overly nervous, they added.
The general index fell 0.18 points, 0.03 percent, to 566.81 and the Ibex rose 3.02 points, 0.05 percent, 6,514.48.
Endesa shed 160 pesetas to 11,140 after it outbid rival BCH group for Retevision, and appeared the likely auction winner, analysts said.
"Clients are not overly nervous as regards Spain, but most of them are taking a wait-and-see stance ahead of next week's (June 16-17 European Union summit) meeting," said a dealer at Merrill Lynch.
He added that until then volume is likely to be trading-based and somewhat volatile, although the Ibex could test the 6,600 level again.
All eyes are still on Friday's May CPI data, with the inflation rate expected to fall to a fresh low of around 1.5 percent year-on-year from 1.7 percent in April.
